title: Acute Hyperkalemia
scenario: A 58-year-old male with a history of chronic kidney disease presents to the emergency department with generalized muscle weakness, fatigue, and palpitations that began this morning. He reports he missed his last two hemodialysis sessions.

lines: 58-year-old male brought in by wife for progressive muscle weakness and palpitations since waking. Reports missing his last two scheduled hemodialysis sessions. Complains of tingling in the lips and fingers. Alert and oriented x3. Deep tendon reflexes diminished. Cardiac monitor applied.
IV access obtained. Stat labs and 12-lead ECG ordered. ECG shows tall, peaked T waves and a widening QRS complex. Provider notified.
Emergency orders received and initiated. IV calcium gluconate, IV regular insulin with dextrose, and nebulized albuterol administered per order. Nephrology consulted for urgent hemodialysis.
Reports weakness improving and palpitations resolved. Repeat ECG shows T waves less peaked and narrowing QRS. Transported to dialysis unit.
Sevelamer 800 mg PO three times daily with meals
Administer calcium gluconate 1 g IV over 2-3 minutes now
Administer regular insulin 10 units IV with 25 g dextrose 50% IV now
Administer albuterol 10 mg via nebulizer now
Repeat potassium and ECG after treatment

children.subject: Medical-Surgical

options.text: Peaked T waves with widening QRS on ECG

children.rationale: A critically high potassium, muscle weakness, characteristic ECG changes, and bradycardia with palpitations all reflect the cardiac and neuromuscular effects of severe hyperkalemia and demand immediate attention.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each finding, click to specify whether it reflects a cardiac effect, a neuromuscular effect, or both of hyperkalemia. Each finding may support more than one.
children.rationale: Elevated potassium alters cardiac conduction (peaked T waves, bradycardia, dysrhythmias) and depresses skeletal muscle and reflex activity (weakness, hyporeflexia).

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse determines that the priority concern for this client is {1}, and the first drug that should be given to address it is {2}.
children.rationale: The priority threat in severe hyperkalemia is a lethal dysrhythmia; IV calcium gluconate is given first to stabilize the cardiac membrane, even though it does not lower potassium.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client.

rows.text: Administer IV regular insulin with dextrose
Prepare the client for urgent hemodialysis
Encourage a diet high in bananas and oranges

children.rationale: Insulin with dextrose shifts potassium into cells, stopping the potassium-raising drugs and dialysis remove the excess. Potassium-containing fluids and high-potassium foods would worsen the imbalance.

children.subject: Pharmacology
children.stem: After administering IV insulin with dextrose for hyperkalemia, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Administer a rapid potassium chloride IV push
Withhold all further monitoring until dialysis
Restrict the client to strict bed rest indefinitely

children.rationale: Insulin drives glucose and potassium into cells, so the nurse watches for hypoglycemia, continues cardiac monitoring, and rechecks potassium. Giving potassium or stopping monitoring would be unsafe.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which findings indicate the treatment for hyperkalemia has been effective? Select all that apply.

options.text: T waves are less peaked and QRS is narrowing
Pulse increased to 72 with resolved palpitations

children.rationale: Improved strength, normalizing ECG, and a return to a normal heart rate show the potassium is falling and cardiac stability is restored. A persistently high potassium or absent reflexes would signal ongoing hyperkalemia.
